methods.name: Peer-Median

private.name: Humanoid

data.narrative:
Aestus Industries is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $10M+. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private robotics firms spanning seed through Series B stages, plus one public comparable, to triangulate fair value.

Two methods were applied. Stage-progression methodology, using total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to next-stage advancement, yielding $20M. Peer-median analysis across five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Humanoid ($1.4B, Series A), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed)—establishes a median valuation of $1.6B, with range $1.1B to $2.0B.

The wide dispersion between methods reflects stage and investor composition differences within the peer set. Stage-progression implies $17M–$20M; peer-median implies $1.1B–$2.0B. The triangulated median of $835M sits between these anchors but is substantially influenced by Series B comparables trading at higher multiples. Key uncertainties include revenue/unit economics at Aestus (not provided), the appropriateness of applying Series B multiples to a Series A target, and whether peer valuations reflect recent market repricing in robotics. A defensible range is $17M–$1.9B, with material sensitivity to stage-adjusted peer selection.
